summary: Fine-tuning makes sense only after prompt engineering and RAG have been exhausted — the canonical 2026 sequence is Prompt → RAG → Fine-tune → Distill, moving right only when the cheaper option provably hits a wall. Most production systems layer all three, with fine-tuning applied specifically when behavior remains inconsistent at scale, a custom style or domain vocabulary must be baked into weights, or latency/cost constraints make runtime retrieval impractical. The bar for needing fine-tuning keeps rising as base models like Qwen3, Llama 4, and Gemma 3 handle out-of-the-box tasks that required fine-tuning 18 months ago.
when_to_fine_tune: Use fine-tuning when prompt engineering and RAG have both been tried and the model still produces inconsistent or off-brand outputs at production scale.
Use fine-tuning when you need to permanently embed domain-specific terminology, tone, or reasoning patterns into model weights rather than injecting them at inference time.
Use fine-tuning when inference latency or cost makes retrieval-augmented approaches impractical, and the knowledge domain is stable enough not to require frequent updates.
Use fine-tuning for RLHF/preference alignment (DPO, PPO, ORPO) when you need the model's default behavior to match human preferences without relying on system prompts.
